items.title: Charlie Gabriel interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 9, 2020
items.q: from what I can understand Freddie Keppard was a member of my grandfather’s band which was the National Jazz Band here in New Orleans in 1920

ctx.x: Can I ask you a question about the music that you were hearing and that your father played and your uncles. Did you call it something? Did you call it jazz? Or was it just —

I have never heard too much of the word jazz until later on after I got to be around 14 or 15, you heard the word jazz. But that word was, from what I can understand Freddie Keppard was a member of my grandfather’s band which was the National Jazz Band here in New Orleans in 1920, see? And he was offered a recording contract to record the music. And Freddie Keppard decided he didn’t want to record the music because he didn’t want them to steal his style of playing. So he put a handkerchief over his finger and he…
What was it like interacting with those older fellas?
